C1803.title: 17-Year-Old Sentenced to Four Years for DDoS Attack on Airline Ticketing System After Failing to Buy Ticket
keywords: 17-year-old sentenced for DDoS attack on ticketing system after failing to buy ticket
crime of damaging computer information systems
C1803.summary: In July 2026, a 17-year-old named Xiao Chen launched a DDoS attack on an airline's ticketing system after failing to purchase a ticket, causing a 4-hour outage affecting 50 million users. He was sentenced to four years in prison by the Guangzhou Baiyun Court for the crime of damaging computer information systems.
C1803.description:
This case is a typical criminal prosecution of a cyberattack triggered by personal frustration. The 17-year-old Xiao Chen, angered by his failure to buy a ticket, used technical means to launch a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack against the airline's ticketing system. The attack flooded the target servers with massive volumes of malicious traffic, exhausting system resources and rendering the service unavailable to legitimate users.

The attack caused a complete paralysis of the ticketing system for four hours, directly affecting approximately 50 million users' normal access and ticket-purchasing operations, inflicting severe economic losses and reputational damage on the airline. The Baiyun District People's Court of Guangzhou determined that Xiao Chen's actions constituted the crime of damaging computer information systems, with particularly serious consequences, and sentenced him to four years in prison according to law.

This case highlights the legal risks of juvenile cybercrime and serves as a warning for enterprises to strengthen anti-DDoS protection for critical business systems. The attacker resorted to extreme measures on a momentary impulse and ultimately paid a heavy legal price.
